newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA CREDIT BANK HAS 435 MLN LVS 96 NET PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA CREDIT BANK HAS 435 MLN LVS 96 NET PROFIT.

text.p: Bulgaria's private Credit Bank posted a 434.6 million lev net profit for 1996 against a 458 million lev loss for 1995, the bank's executive director said on Tuesday.
"The bank has a net profit of 434.6 million levs for last year, which would be used to cover the loss for the previous year under today's decision of bank shareholders," Evgeni Goranov told repoters.
The shareholders also decided to raise capital to 30 billion levs from 10 billion levs through a new share issue.
After the rise the capital would be distributed into 30.2 million levs of voting shares and 29.8 million of non-voting shares with a par of 500 levs each.
The bank's assets totalled 54.6 billion levs and its capital to risk assets ratio was 2.29 percent at end-1996, figures showed.
Its liabilities to other financial institutions and clients amounted to 32.7 billion levs.

Credit bank was set up six years ago as a leading banking instition of Bulgaria's business conglomerate Multigroup. The bank has been licensed for domestic and international banking operations by Bulgaria's central bank.

The shareholders' meeting replaced Ciela consultancy firm and Evgeni Goranov as board members with Vesselin Blagoev, former executive director of Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency, and Ivailo Bozhkov, so far Credit bank procurator.
Blagoev and Bozhkov were also appointed as two of the four execuitive directors of Credit bank.
"I resigned from the bank but I will remain with Multigroup structures," Goranov said.

Last year gas company Overgas Inc, a joint venture between Multigoup structures and Russia's gas monopolist Gazprom acquired five percent of Credit bank voting shares. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
